record.paper_title: Open Problem: Average-Case Hardness of Hypergraphic Planted Clique Detection
record.original_question: For hypergraphic planted clique detection, let a d-hypergraph be an order-d extension of a graph, let G_d(N, 1/2) be the Erdos-Renyi d-hypergraph on N vertices with each d-vertex hyperedge independently present with probability 1/2, and let G_d(N, 1/2, kappa) be the model obtained by choosing kappa vertices uniformly at random and adding every hyperedge whose vertices all lie in that planted set. Given the adjacency tensor A of the observed hypergraph, what is the sharp threshold for the planted clique size kappa that guarantees that HPC can be solved by singular value decomposition after matricizing or unfolding A, and is there another polynomial-time algorithm for HPC that succeeds below that SVD threshold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $d\ge 2$. A $d$-hypergraph on vertex set $[N]=\{1,\dots,N\}$ is a set of $d$-element subsets of $[N]$ (its hyperedges). Define the Erdős–Rényi $d$-hypergraph $G_d(N,1/2)$ to be the random $d$-hypergraph in which each of the $\binom{N}{d}$ possible hyperedges is included independently with probability $1/2$. For an integer $\kappa\in\{d,\dots,N\}$, define the planted model $G_d(N,1/2,\kappa)$ as follows: sample $G\sim G_d(N,1/2)$, choose a subset $S\subset[N]$ with $|S|=\kappa$ uniformly at random, and add to $G$ every $d$-subset of $S$ (if not already present), producing a hypergraph in which $S$ induces a complete sub-$d$-hypergraph (a planted $\kappa$-clique). The observation is the symmetric order-$d$ adjacency tensor $A\in\{0,1\}^{N\times\cdots\times N}$ of the resulting hypergraph.

The hypergraphic planted clique detection problem (HPC) is the hypothesis testing problem of distinguishing $H_0:A\sim G_d(N,1/2)$ from $H_1:A\sim G_d(N,1/2,\kappa)$ with vanishing total error as $N\to\infty$.

(a) Determine the sharp asymptotic threshold $\kappa^{\mathrm{SVD}}_d(N)$ such that the following holds: if $\kappa/\kappa^{\mathrm{SVD}}_d(N)\to\infty$ then HPC can be solved with high probability by computing the singular value decomposition of some matricization (unfolding) of $A$ into a matrix and thresholding its leading singular value, whereas if $\kappa/\kappa^{\mathrm{SVD}}_d(N)\to 0$ then no such SVD-of-unfolding test succeeds.

(b) Decide whether there exists a polynomial-time algorithm (in $N$) that solves HPC with high probability for some clique size $\kappa$ strictly below the threshold $\kappa^{\mathrm{SVD}}_d(N)$ identified in (a).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., a 2026 arXiv preprint on planted clique detection from the hypergraph adjacency matrix) studies spectral tests at the √N scale for related models and develops polynomial-time spectral methods, but does not establish a sharp SVD threshold for general order-d HPC nor exhibit a polynomial-time algorithm provably succeeding below the SVD/unfolding threshold. The question of computational hardness equivalence between HPC and standard planted clique remains a stated open direction. No source found resolving the sharp κ threshold or beating it in polynomial time.

status_evidence.title: Planted clique detection and recovery from the hypergraph adjacency matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral norm test is asymptotically powerful at the √n scale; polynomial-time spectral method achieves exact recovery at the canonical √n scale.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work provides spectral algorithms at √N scale but does not establish a sharp threshold or beat the SVD threshold for general d.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Average-Case Hardness of Hypergraphic Planted Clique Detection
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem posed regarding sharp κ threshold for HPC detection via SVD/unfolding and existence of better polynomial-time algorithms.
status_evidence.claim: The problem was posed as open.
